definitions.gloss: to rush someone, to hurry someone along, to urge haste
definitions.explanation: To pressure or urge someone to do something faster. The subject pushes another person to hurry up.

examples.japanese: そんなに{急|せ}かさないでください。
examples.english: Please don't rush me like that.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}に{急|せ}かされて{家|いえ}を{出|で}た。
examples.english: My mother rushed me out of the house.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りが{近|ちか}いと、{上司|じょうし}が{毎日|まいにち}のように{急|せ}かしてくる。
examples.english: When the deadline is approaching, my boss rushes me almost every day.

notes:
USAGE:
Always directed at another person — you {急|せ}かす someone else. Often appears in the passive form {急|せ}かされる (to be rushed by someone). Carries a mildly negative nuance of unwanted pressure.

GRAMMAR:
Godan verb ending in す. Transitive — takes を for the person being rushed: Xを{急|せ}かす.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急|せ}かさないで: don't rush me
- {急|せ}かされる: to be rushed (passive)
- {返事|へんじ}を{急|せ}かす: to press for a reply
